glosses: to unpack (to remove from a package or container)

examples.text: Kasia jak każde dziecko uwielbiała rozpakowywać świąteczne prezenty.
examples.translation: Like every child, Kasia loved opening Christmas presents.
examples.english: Like every child, Kasia loved opening Christmas presents.

glosses: to zip (to convert a computer file into a smaller package)
to unpack (to empty one's packed belongings)

examples.text: Jest Jerzy? Tak, rozpakowuje się na górze.
examples.translation: Is Jerzy here? Yes, he's upstairs unpacking.
examples.english: Is Jerzy here? Yes, he's upstairs unpacking.

glosses: To remove from a package or container, particularly with respect to items that had previously been arranged closely and securely in a pack.

examples.text: They didn't have time to unpack their bags before going out to dinner.

glosses: To empty containers that had been packed.

examples.text: They didn't have time to unpack before going to dinner.

glosses: To analyze a concept or a text; to explain.

examples.text: There may be another argument here, if we had time to unpack it, about modernism and the rise of the middle classes.
Yet few Americans — including the president — understand how global trade works, both how it can help our economy and how some can be left behind. Let’s try to unpack a few of the complexities.
From a gender reveal to a secret ceremony and rifts with other royal family members, there was a lot to unpack from the interview

glosses: To undergo separation of its features into distinct segments.

examples.text: The rounded vowels [y] and [œ/ə] in Russian seem to unpack as glide-vowel sequences in words borrowed from French and German, […]

Whereas the high vowels /ʏ, y/ unpack, the mid vowels /œ, ø/ are adapted as single segments in these languages (see examples in (36) for Vietnamese (Barker 1969) and (37) for Fon (Gbeto 2000)). […]

accu [a'ky] → ac-quy [ak kwi]
